claims.text: SPS consolidation at 1500°C improves the molten-aluminum corrosion resistance of ZrB2-AlFeNiCoCr cermets.
The improvement from SPS at 1500°C is caused by optimized binder fluidity and densification.
The proposed cermet contains ZrB2 powder with a particle size of 1–5 μm and 30% AlFeNiCoCr binder.
The AlFeNiCoCr binder is prepared from equimolar quantities of Al, Fe, Ni, Co, and Cr.
The specified SPS process uses vacuum, 50 MPa pressure, an approximately 200°C/min heating rate, and a 5-minute hold at 1500°C.
The relevant corrosion environment is molten aluminum at 700°C for exposure periods up to 12 days.
At 1500°C, the high-entropy-alloy binder is liquid and uniformly infiltrates pores in the cermet.
Binder infiltration at 1500°C strongly connects the ZrB2 grains.
SPS at 1500°C produces the highest relative density, approximately 97.71%, and a compact microstructure.
Effective pore filling and grain bonding minimize connected pathways for molten-aluminum penetration.
Reducing molten-aluminum penetration suppresses ZrB2 grain detachment.
Reducing molten-aluminum penetration decreases the formation of Al-rich reaction products.
The microstructure produced at 1500°C improves hardness and fracture toughness.
Cermets sintered at 1500°C will have superior density to otherwise comparable cermets sintered at 1300°C, 1400°C, or 1600°C.
Cermets sintered at 1500°C will have greater hardness and fracture toughness than samples sintered at 1300°C, 1400°C, or 1600°C.
Cermets sintered at 1500°C will have lower molten-aluminum corrosion rates than samples sintered at 1300°C, 1400°C, or 1600°C.
Cermets sintered at 1500°C will exhibit lower wear volume and more stable friction behavior than samples sintered at the other evaluated temperatures.
The fracture toughness of the 1500°C cermet may exceed that of pure ZrB2, whose reference fracture toughness is approximately 4.5 MPa·m^1/2.
The asserted performance range is limited to the 30% binder composition, the stated SPS parameters, molten-aluminum exposure at 700°C for up to 12 days, and the specified room-temperature wear test.

The hypothesis is falsified if the 1500°C samples lack statistically significant improvements in density, mechanical properties, corrosion resistance, and wear performance relative to all three temperature controls.
